bullets.title: NVDA: FY28 guidance raised ~75% but stock falls on CEO exit, China chip halt, SEC probe
bullets.body: NVDA beat Q3 and raised FY28 revenue growth guidance to ~75% (from ~70%), with demand exceeding supply, but the stock fell ~2.9% as multiple headwinds offset the beat: board won't reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO (ARM's Rene Haas approached for the role), Hopper/H200 chip sales to China halted amid Congressional scrutiny over military diversion, and SEC opened a civil probe. Summit Insights Group downgraded to Hold. NVDA is executing a $150B buyback authorization at ~$45B/quarter through FY28-end while supporting $118B in supplier/data center commitments.

bullets.title: CRDO: Q3 beat and third consecutive guidance raise on AI momentum
bullets.body: Credo Technology (ticker shown as 'P'/Everpure in sources but metrics match CRDO) posted Q3 revenue of $1.46B vs. consensus $1.33B and EPS $0.86 vs. $0.78, with product revenue a particular standout at $947M vs. $807M expected. Full-year revenue guidance raised to $5.20-5.21B from $5.03-5.07B, and operating income guidance raised to $1.08-1.09B from $940-960M prior; management reiterated a strong preliminary FY28 outlook.

bullets.title: NET: Q1 beat, FY ARR guidance raised to 26%, acquires Applied Compute for $4.5B
bullets.body: Cloudflare reported Q1 revenue of $3.44B (vs. $3.31B consensus) and EPS $1.05 (vs. $0.97), with Next Gen ARR of $9.73B and total RPO of $21B. FY ARR guidance raised from 22% to 26%. The company announced a $4.5B all-stock acquisition of Applied Compute to support enterprise AI security, expected to close April 2027; operating margin held at 29.5% and FCF margin at 38%.

bullets.title: MU: 75% of 2027 supply sold out; 2027-28 expected tighter than record 2026
bullets.body: Micron at TomorrowX Summit highlighted AI-driven memory demand with 75% of 2027 supply already committed and 2028 discussions underway. Management expects 2027 to be stronger than record 2026, with 2027-28 even tighter; multiyear take-or-pay agreements with ~5-year terms and cash deposits provide visibility. Stacked 3D DRAM seen as next major wave entering market ~2028-29. CHIPS Act restrictions expire Dec 9; company intends to return excess cash to shareholders.

bullets.title: AMD: OpenAI partnership delivers 14% PPA improvement on GPU chip design in <5 months
bullets.body: OpenAI's AI-driven SystemVerilog RTL rewrite of AMD GPU IP achieved up to 14% performance-per-watt improvement versus the typical ~1-year design cycle, accomplished in under 5 months. AMD has already incorporated the changes into recent manufacturing designs and future production files, suggesting meaningful efficiency gains in upcoming GPU generations.

bullets.title: INTC: Server CPU demand meaningfully exceeds supply through 2027-28; capex doubling in 4Q
bullets.body: UBS sales notes from IR call series flag Intel server CPU demand materially outstripping supply, expected to persist through 2027 and into 2028. 4Q capex doubling to $8B sequentially ($20B guided for the year) with prepayments on substrate suppliers. Intel 3 process critical for Granite/Nova Lake/Clearwater Forest/Diamond Rapids; Clearwater Forest has 2.5x demand vs. Intel supply. 600bps sequential gross margin drop in 4Q driven by volume (200bps), mix (200bps), and an Israel accident (200bps).

bullets.title: MSFT: Ackman clarifies bullish position — bought 2M deep ITM calls despite selling shares
bullets.body: Bill Ackman sold ~2M MSFT shares in the SeptQ 13F but simultaneously purchased 2M deep in-the-money OTC call options (~$310 strike, 2.5-year term) in July for portfolio management reasons. Ackman remains bullish and believes the stock is undervalued; Pershing Square's net economic exposure is effectively unchanged. Separately, ByteDance is in talks to expand its Microsoft Azure/OpenAI contract by $500M.

bullets.title: FOXA/ROKU: Newsmax files antitrust lawsuit seeking divestiture of Tubi or The Roku Channel
bullets.body: Newsmax Broadcasting filed a federal antitrust suit in the Northern District of California alleging Fox's $22B Roku acquisition violates Section 7 of the Clayton Act by creating an effective monopoly in FAST (free ad-supported streaming TV). Newsmax is seeking injunctive relief, independent Roku management, and divestiture of either Tubi or The Roku Channel. FOXA fell 1.5% on the news; this is Newsmax's second antitrust action against Fox.

bullets.title: GOOGL: +0.8% as Waymo CA highway ban offset by new agentic Gemini features
bullets.body: Google was modestly positive on the day despite Waymo temporarily removing vehicles from California highways after a state ban; management rolled out new agentic Gemini features. Avory CIO Emory highlighted Alphabet (alongside Amazon) as a structural hyperscaler winner controlling AI infrastructure and customer relationships, with advantages over pure-play AI model companies.

bullets.title: DIS: Citi Buy/$140 PT; management confident in double-digit EPS growth via 'One Disney'
bullets.body: Following a meeting with CEO and CFO, Citi maintained its Buy rating and $140 PT on Disney, implying ~21% total return. Management cited satisfaction with FY26 results and confidence in long-term double-digit Adj EPS growth via the 'One Disney' strategy leveraging theme parks (13 cruise ships by 2032), streaming ($3B cost savings to reinvest in Disney+ content), and dynamic pricing. Disney domestic parks per-capita spend rose +4% with +3% attendance.

bullets.title: CHTR: Completes $2.72B tender offer at ~55% of par, capturing $1.22B debt discount
bullets.body: Charter accepted $2.72B face value of senior secured notes for $1.50B cash (blended ~55% of par), capturing a pre-tax debt discount of $1.22B or ~$7.39/share. Settlement occurs November 19, 2026. The transaction represents meaningful balance sheet optimization at a time of elevated rate pressure on the cable sector.

bullets.title: DKNG: Michigan October GGR -18% YoY; market share slips to 28% from 29%
bullets.body: Michigan October sports betting GGR fell 3% YoY overall, with DraftKings posting a sharper -18% GGR decline and handle down 4% YoY; market share slipped to 28% from 29%. Promotional intensity increased (promos rose to 4.0% from 2.6%). FanDuel (-7%) and BetMGM (-18%) also fell; iGaming was the bright spot at +14% YoY overall.

bullets.title: GEV: Downgraded to Hold at Erste Group; participating in GS Industrials Conference Dec 2-3
bullets.body: GE Vernova was downgraded to Hold from Buy at Erste Group, with the stock down 1.0% on the session. The company is confirmed as a presenter at the Goldman Sachs Industrials and Materials Conference in New York on December 2-3.

bullets.title: ENPH/FSLR: Jefferies sees value in both if 45X tax credit scope expands; ENPH director selling 1M shares
bullets.body: Jefferies flagged value in Enphase and First Solar contingent on potential expansion of the 45X manufacturing tax credit. Separately, an ENPH director filed notice to sell 1.0M shares, sending the stock down 1.7% on the day.

bullets.title: WULF: TeraWulf positioned as AI power-shell provider at Morgan Stanley Powering AI Summit (Dec 2)
bullets.body: TeraWulf CEO Paul Prager is a featured speaker at the Morgan Stanley Powering AI Summit on December 2, where the company will host 1x1 meetings. TeraWulf is positioned as a power shell provider transitioning from Bitcoin mining to AI data center hosting, a key theme at the event focused on AI infrastructure constraints.

bullets.title: YELP: Cuts ~5% workforce; reinvests savings in AI; trading at 3.4x NTM EV/EBITDA vs 5.4x median
bullets.body: Yelp announced a ~5% workforce reduction with $14-16M in estimated charges (mostly 4Q26-1Q27), while reiterating 2026 revenue guidance of $1.455-1.460B and adjusted EBITDA of $320-325M. Majority of savings will be reinvested in high-return AI opportunities. The stock trades at 3.4x NTM EV/EBITDA versus a three-year median of 5.4x.

bullets.title: NVDA ecosystem: Citi names DDOG, CRWD, RBRK as cyber-resilience beneficiaries; FTNT on OT/IoT
bullets.body: Citi's systems software note flags tech outages as a structural tailwind for observability (DDOG, DT), backup/recovery (RBRK), and multi-platform cyber vendors (CRWD). OT/IoT security is gaining urgency with FTNT having 15-20% exposure; NOW (via Armis) and ZS are secondary beneficiaries. On-premise deployments gaining appeal as AI risk mitigation, benefiting CRWD, ZS, and RBRK sovereign data center buildouts.

bullets.title: ARM: CEO Rene Haas approached by NVDA board's recruitment firm for CEO role
bullets.body: ARM CEO Rene Haas has been approached by Nvidia's board recruitment firm as the company searches for a new CEO following Jensen Huang's departure. No indication Haas has accepted or is in advanced discussions. The development adds uncertainty to both ARM's leadership continuity and NVDA's post-Jensen transition timeline.

bullets.title: U (Unity): Confirmed at JPM Digital Apps & Video Gaming Summit Dec 7 with CFO
bullets.body: Unity Software is confirmed at JPMorgan's December 7 Digital Apps & Video Gaming Summit in New York, with CFO Jarrod Yahes and VP Alex Giaimo attending. Take-Two Interactive (with GTA VI scoring 99 on Metacritic) is also confirmed. Registration deadline is EOD Thursday, November 19.

bullets.title: DIS macro read: AI tools cutting costs; parks spend resilient; fuel/freight headwind building
bullets.body: Disney cut film rendering compute needs 30% with AI tools. Domestic parks per-capita spend +4% with +3% attendance. Broad consumer earnings (TJX, TGT, HD, LOW) show fuel and freight as the emerging Q4 margin headwind — TJX flagged 50bps adjusted GM drop, Lowe's diesel +15% vs Q2 drove ~30bps GM pressure, HD flagged unplanned inflation in fuel/energy/resin/metals at -60bps GM y/y — while AI tools (Mylow, Ask Target, HD search) are driving meaningful online conversion gains.
